messages:
Maya: quick q — we have a handful of clients that send both Authorization: Bearer <token> and X-Api-Key: <key> in the same request. how should middleware decide which to use for org/project scoping?

Raj: prefer Authorization for authn/authz. treat X-Api-Key as project-scoped fallback only if Authorization is missing or token is service-level without project claims.

Sam: ok but we need clear precedence for rate limits and billing attribution. which header wins for billing?

Raj: billing follows the identity used for the request. if Authorization is valid and maps to an org/project, bill that. if Authorization is absent/invalid and X-Api-Key resolves to a project, bill the project from the key. otherwise anonymous.

Alicia: security note — if both present and they mismatch (different orgs), we should 403 rather than using one silently. failure mode: explicit deny when conflicting identities.

Maya: +1 on 403 for mismatch. what about legacy SDKs that rely on X-Project header (x-project-id) instead of embedding project in key? we still support it, right?

Raj: support for X-Project-id stays for the deprecation window. precedence order we propose: 1) Authorization bearer token (if has project/org claims) 2) X-Project-Id header (explicit project override) 3) X-Api-Key project mapping 4) anonymous. If two different project sources disagree -> 403.

Sam: that ordering seems fine, but must document it and add tests. also need to clarify 401 vs 403 semantics around key rotation/gaps.

Alicia: rotation: we want a soft-grace period where recently-rotated keys still accept both old and new for 24h, but treat old-key usage as "stale" in logs. For expired keys -> 401. For mismatched org/project -> 403.

Maya: can we show an example curl and the expected response when both headers present and match vs mismatch?

Raj: example (match):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ey...token-with-project-123' \n  -H 'X-Api-Key: pk_live_abc123' \n  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Response: 200 OK, body contains generation, billing attributed to project from token.

Raj: example (mismatch):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ey...token-project-123' \n  -H 'X-Api-Key: pk_live_xyz789' \n  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Response: 403 Forbidden, body: {"error":"conflicting-project-assertions","message":"Authorization token and X-Api-Key resolve to different projects"}

Sam: what about clients that send Authorization but token lacks project claim? fallback to X-Api-Key or X-Project-Id?

Raj: yes fallback to X-Project-Id first, then X-Api-Key. If no project info anywhere, treat as org-level token if allowed, else 401. We'll add a clear rule table in the spec.

Maya: middleware change plan:
- decode Authorization if present
- if token invalid -> return 401 (unless key can authenticate)
- resolve project from token -> if present use it
- else if X-Project-Id present -> use it
- else if X-Api-Key present -> lookup key -> if key maps to project use it
- if multiple sources present and disagree -> 403
- propagate identity headers downstream: X-RW-Principal, X-RW-Project, X-RW-Org

Sam: tiny nit — when token invalid we should still allow evaluation of X-Api-Key (so clients can rotate tokens without downtime). return 401 only if no alternate header authenticates. so try all auth methods before 401, but short-circuit to 403 on explicit conflict.

Raj: agreed. implement as "try authenticate with each method -> collect asserted identities -> if zero -> 401 -> if one -> use it -> if >1 and all equal -> use it -> if >1 and differ -> 403"

Alicia: please add observability hooks: log which header resolved identity, mark "resolution_source" in traces, and emit metric auth.resolution_conflicts. Also flag stale-key usage during rotation.

Maya: added docs TODO, tests, and a middleware PR draft. pinging @Raj for code review and @Alicia for security signoff.

Maya: @Raj PTAL at https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/inference/merge_requests/432 (middleware: auth/resolve -> precedence + conflict test cases). summary in MR description.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for MR 432 — unit tests running. :gear:

Raj: will review today. plan to add a unit test that simulates conflicting claims and asserts 403 + audit log entry.

Sam: also let's add an integration test that covers token-without-project + X-Api-Key fallback to ensure no regression.

Alicia: schedule security review: I'll review MR and threat model on rotation handling. target deadline EOD Thu.

Maya: thanks — once reviews + tests pass we'll announce deprecation timeline for X-Project-Id header (60 days notice) and publish migration steps for SDKs.

Maya: putting this on the eng-platform board as a task: ENGPLAT-827.

Raj: sounds good. I'll comment on MR with the exact rule table and add the metrics hooks.

Maya: awesome. closing the loop here — follow up in MR and changelog. :thumbsup:
